message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated composers who have made their mark in the United States—spanning from early pioneers to modern innovators:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz‑Classical Fusion | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Neoclassical/“American” Sound | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Broadway & Classical | *West Side Story*, *Candide* (score) |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film Scores | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Modernist | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Postminimalism | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **William Grant Still** (1895‑1978) | “First Black Classical Composer” | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird* |

These figures represent just a slice of the rich tapestry of American composition—from early ragtime and jazz influences to contemporary minimalism and film scoring. Each has helped shape what we think of as “American music” today.
